book.unit_title: Introduction to Career and Technical Education (CTE)

title: Meaning of Career and Technical Education

keywords.def: Teaching skills-based careers to students. Short form: CTE.
Education whose main purpose is learning.
Education that focuses on practical skills for doing a task.
The knowledge, skills and attitudes needed at work.

en.text: Career and Technical Education, or CTE, joins academic education and technical education. Academic education has learning as its main purpose. Technical education focuses on practical skills for a task. CTE prepares students for further education and for the world of work.

screens.title: Phones and maths
screens.ask: A school teaches students to repair phones and also to read and do maths. What kind of education is this?
screens.after: It joins learning with practical skills. That is the idea of CTE.

screens.title: 1.3 Meaning of CTE
paras: Career and Technical Education (CTE) combines academic and technical skills.
It gives the knowledge and training needed for further education and jobs.
It teaches technology-based and career-oriented skills.
CTE offers skills to begin working in different economic sectors.

screens.title: Two kinds of education
paras: CTE combines academic education and technical education.
table: Focuses on practical or technical skills for a task.
Example: metal work, hairdressing, farming skills.

screens.title: Ready for work
paras: CTE prepares students for the world of work.
It introduces workplace competencies: knowledge, skills and attitudes.
Students practise them in a real-world, applied context.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Teaching skills-based careers to students. Short form: CTE.
Education whose main purpose is learning.
Education that focuses on practical skills for doing a task.
The knowledge, skills and attitudes needed at work.

screens.text: CTE combines which two kinds of education?
screens.why: CTE joins academic learning with technical skills.

items: A practical skill for a task.
screens.why: Academic = learning as the main aim. Technical = practical skills for a task.
screens.clue: Is the main aim knowing, or doing a task?

screens.text: Is education from Grade 1–6 mainly academic or technical?
screens.why: Grades 1–6 mostly teach reading, writing, maths and science: learning is the main purpose.
screens.clue: What is the main purpose of those grades?

screens.ask: Workplace competencies are knowledge, skills and ___.
screens.why: The book lists knowledge, skills and attitudes.
screens.clue: Think about how you behave at work.

screens.text: CTE does not involve acquiring knowledge.
screens.why: CTE combines academic knowledge with technical skills.
screens.clue: What does the A in "academic" side bring?

screens.text: Tigist learns maths in class and then uses it to measure cloth in a tailoring workshop. Which part of CTE does the workshop show?
opts: Applying knowledge in a real-world context
screens.ans: Applying knowledge in a real-world context
screens.why: CTE introduces workplace competencies in a real-world, applied context. She uses classroom maths for a real task.
screens.clue: Where is she using what she learned?

test.text: Technical education focuses on practical skills for doing a task.
Education whose main purpose is learning is called:
test.why: Academic = learning is the main aim.

test.ask: CTE prepares students for further education and for the world of ___.
test.why: CTE prepares students for the world of work.
Competencies are knowledge, skills and attitudes.

notes.text: Activity 3 is open; asked as a choice with the book-based model answer (mainly academic).
The academic/technical examples in the table are added for clarity.
